title: Leicester Lancaster Memorial

external_narratives.summary: IWM registers a wall-mounted plaque commemorating the airmen of 300 Polish Bomber Squadron killed when Lancaster PA269 crashed on Long Street, Wigston, Leicester on 4 February 1946. All six crew members were killed.
key_details: Crash location was Long Street, Wigston
external_narratives.link_description: A wall-mounted plaque honoring fallen airmen at Leicester's Lancaster Memorial.

external_narratives.summary: A second IWM-registered memorial -- a commemorative tree -- also marks the site of the Lancaster PA269 crash in Wigston, providing a living memorial alongside the plaque.
external_narratives.link_description: A poignant tree memorial honoring the Lancaster PA269 crash victims at Leicester's Wigston.

external_narratives.summary: In February 2026, Oadby and Wigston Borough Council marked the 80th anniversary of the crash. The Lancaster, on a routine flight from RAF Faldingworth, was believed to have been hit by lightning during a violent thunderstorm. The pilot, Wing Commander Romuald Sulinski KSOVM DSO DFC, avoided Long Street and the nearby school, steering towards a ploughed field. The aircraft crashed at approximately 13:25, missing Long Street Modern School by less than 10 feet.
key_details: Pilot was Wg Cdr Sulinski DSO DFC
Missed school by less than 10 feet
Crew buried at Newark-Upon-Trent Polish war graves
external_narratives.link_description: Explore Leicester Lancaster Memorial's history and significance at Oadby and Wigston Borough Council's 80th anniversary event in February 2026.

external_narratives.summary: War Memorials Online registers the Faldingworth memorial to 300 Squadron Polish Air Force, providing broader context for the Polish squadron's presence in Lincolnshire and their post-war losses.
external_narratives.link_description: The Faldingworth Memorial honoring 300 Squadron Polish Air Force on War Memorials Online.

memorial_details:
Name: Polish aircrew - Avro Lancaster PA269
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: Wall mounted rectangular reflective steel plaque commemorating the airmen of 300 Polish Bomber Squadron killed in a crash on 4th February 1946. Polish Air Force crest at top left, 300 Squadron crest at top centre and Royal Air Force crest at top right of plaque: all crests have identifying names immediately beneath them. Dedication is below the crests, and names are set out in two columns of three names each below the dedication. All crests and lettering are in the same mid-blue colour. Note: This memorial is in a school building - there is also a beech tree in the school grounds planted to commemorate the same incident (see memorial reference 55367).
Inscription: THIS PLAQUE HAS BEEN ERECTED IN MEMORY OF THE AIRMEN OF/ 300 POLISH SQUADRON WHO, WHILST FLYING LANCASTER BOMBER A1 PA 269/ OVER LEICESTER ON 4th FEBRUARY 1946 CRASHED ON THIS SCHOOL SITE/ KILLING THE FOLLOWING CREW MEMBERS/ [crew names inscribed on memorial]
Location: All Saints Church of England Primary School Long Street Wigston Magna Oadby And Wigston Leicestershire LE18 2AH England
Grid Ref: SP 60505 98957
Coordinates: 52.585222450937,-1.108995200000
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/59/405/55366_plaque.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/59/406/55366_ready_for_unveiling.jpg
narrative: Lancaster PA269, crewed by six Polish airmen of 300 (Masovia) Squadron PAF from Faldingworth, was on a routine flight when it crashed at Wigston, Leicester, on 4 February 1946. The aircraft is believed to have been struck by lightning during a violent thunderstorm. With the bomber ablaze, the crew steered it away from the streets and houses below, directing it toward a ploughed field behind Long Street Modern School — missing the building by less than ten feet. All six crew members were killed: W. Brzezinski, W. Jedrzejczyk, F. Mikula, C. Sulgut, R. Sulinski, and M. Szwandt. Their actions prevented casualties among the 80 children sheltering inside the school at the moment of impact. Some residents suffered minor injuries, but there were no deaths on the ground.
inscription:
THIS PLAQUE HAS BEEN ERECTED IN MEMORY OF THE AIRMEN OF
300 POLISH SQUADRON WHO, WHILST FLYING LANCASTER BOMBER A1 PA 269
OVER LEICESTER ON 4th FEBRUARY 1946 CRASHED ON THIS SCHOOL SITE
KILLING THE FOLLOWING CREW MEMBERS

memorial_name: 300 Polish Bomber Squadron: Lancaster PA269 crash - tree
memorial_description: Beech tree planted in school grounds on the site where a Lancaster PA269 being flown by members of 300 Polish Bomber Squadron crashed in 1946. Note: There is also a plaque inside the school commemorating this incident which bears the names of the six airmen who were killed - see memorial reference 55366.
